title: Feammox Metagenome
description: Nitrogen is essential for life, but human activities alter its cycle, affecting several ecosystems. Conventional biological nitrogen removal treatments, such as nitrification and denitrification, have limitations due to the high demand for oxygen and the need for exogenous carbon. As alternatives, the Anammox and Feammox processes have gained attention, although Anammox faces challenges due to the short lifespan of nitrite and bacterial inhibition by high concentrations of organic matter. In this study, the Feammox process was evaluated, which can operate under anaerobic and heterotrophic conditions. Experimental results indicate that it was possible to enrich Feammox from Anammox sludge by modifying the environmental conditions. Co-removal of ammonium and organic carbon was observed at lower concentrations of Fe3+ (200 mg/L), showing that the Feammox process can not only occur under autotrophic conditions, but also at low concentrations of Fe3+. This suggests potential coupling with Fe2+ oxidation processes and Fe cycling. Furthermore, PCR analysis revealed the presence of key genes and microorganisms, such as Geobacter spp., Shewanella spp., Ferrovum myxofaciens, Albidiferax ferrireducens, and Acidimicrobium, suggesting that the experimental conditions favored Feammox activity and that the Anammox inoculum was suitable for its enrichment. The results indicate that it is possible to obtain a microbial community with Feammox activity at low iron concentrations and high organic carbon concentrations, and that the Feammox process can be viable at low Fe3+ concentrations, which would be crucial for its scaling
